body_swap:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the target character from <Picture 1>, retaining its identity, facial structure, proportions, colors and clothing. <Video 1> is the sole source of body movement, facial performance, camera, cuts and timing.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. <Subject 1> reproduces the source dancer’s physical and facial performance at the same timing and intensity, retaining the source setting and lighting.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1>: fully_preserved — target identity and appearance.
<Video 1>: attribute_transfer — choreography, exact facial states, articulation, gaze, camera and timing; fully_preserved — physical environment and lighting; partially_preserved — dancer replaced by <Subject 1>.

detailed_description:
From the opening frame through the ending, <Subject 1> follows the source dancer’s position, steps, gestures, turns and pauses. At each moment, the face matches the source’s visible expression, including its intensity, duration and transitions. Neutral or still facial intervals remain equally neutral or still. Eyebrow position, eyelid opening, gaze, cheek tension, mouth-corner position, lip shape and jaw opening follow the source at the same timing and amplitude. Closed-mouth intervals remain closed; visible articulation follows the source syllable rhythm and pauses. The reference image supplies facial identity; the video supplies every expression. Preserve this correspondence through head turns, occlusions and cuts. Hair, clothing and accessories follow the body’s movement. Preserve source framing, camera movement, cut sequence and final pose. Scene surfaces extend cleanly across the full frame.

N/A.
